message.content:
Let \(t=\cos x\). Since \(x\) is real, \(t\in[-1,1]\).

Also,
\[
\cos 2x=2\cos^2x-1=2t^2-1.
\]
So
\[
f(x)=2t^2-1-2a(1+t)
=2t^2-2at-2a-1.
\]
Define
\[
g(t)=2t^2-2at-2a-1,\qquad t\in[-1,1].
\]

This is an upward-opening quadratic. Its vertex occurs at
\[
t=\frac{2a}{4}=\frac a2.
\]
If \(\frac a2\in[-1,1]\), then the minimum occurs at \(t=\frac a2\). The minimum value is
\[
g\left(\frac a2\right)
=2\left(\frac a2\right)^2-2a\left(\frac a2\right)-2a-1
=-\frac{a^2}{2}-2a-1.
\]
Set this equal to \(-\frac12\):
\[
-\frac{a^2}{2}-2a-1=-\frac12.
\]
Multiply by \(-2\):
\[
a^2+4a+1=0.
\]
Thus
\[
a=-2\pm\sqrt3.
\]
For the minimum to occur at \(t=\frac a2\), we need \(\frac a2\in[-1,1]\), i.e. \(-2\le a\le 2\). The value
\[
a=-2-\sqrt3
\]
is less than \(-2\), so it is not valid. The other value is
\[
a=-2+\sqrt3.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{-2+\sqrt3}\).
